The root cause is in opentui's ScrollBox, not opencode. PR #722 fixed one code path but two remained: missing _hasManualScroll guards in recalculateBarProps else branch, and no reset of _hasManualScroll when scrolling back to the sticky edge. This PR worked around it by attempting to snap to bottom within 5 lines. The TUI-side fix in opentui #1088 corrects this within 1 line. Filed opentui #1087 with the issue and opentui #1088 with a proposed fix. Verified working in a patched local build.

I read through the code and traced all three impact paths. I wanted to verify impact path 2 concretely before commenting, so I added a temporary patch to `ignore()` that forces it to always return an empty `Set` — simulating what happens when `git check-ignore` exits with a non-0/non-1 code. **Instrumented reproduction of impact path 2** Steps: 1. Let the AI create `secret.txt` with no `.gitignore` present — the file gets staged into the snapshot index via `add()` 2. Added `secret.txt` to `.gitignore` 3. Ran `/undo` The backend log confirmed `ignore()` was returning empty on every call: Before `/undo`, `secret.txt` is present alongside `.gitignore`: After `/undo`, `secret.txt` is deleted from disk: This confirms the impact path 2 chain: `ignore()` returns empty → `secret.txt` is not filtered out of the `Patch` → `revert()` finds it absent from the snapshot hash → `fs.remove()` deletes it. **Note on real-world trigger** This simulation forces the failure unconditionally. In production the trigger is a non-0/non-1 exit from `git check-ignore` — exit code 128 on Windows under path-length pressure, lock contention, or a malformed `.gitignore`. The current code has no log entry at that point, so the failure is invisible until files start disappearing. **Planned fix** I'll implement Option A. On a non-0/non-1 exit, return `new Set(files)` instead of `new Set()`: ```typescript if (check.code !== 0 && check.code !== 1) { log.warn("git check-ignore failed, treating all candidates as ignored for safety", { exitCode: check.code, stderr: check.stderr, fileCount: files.length, }) return new Set(files) } ``` I'll also add an `ignore()` filter to `diff()` output to close impact path 3.

FWIW `gcompat` is an ugly hack so we can run closed source binaries that only build against GNU libc. For open source software there are no good reason to need gcompat because you can build from source.

And for precompiled binaries, it is usually better to provide statically compiled binaries to avoid problems like this - and musl is really good at statically compiled bins.

And if you need `dlopen`, for plugins, I would still think it would be a good idea to build against musl, and ship musl libc with the precompiled binary. You can run a musl linked binary with `./libc.so /path/to/binary` where `libc.so` is musl.

I don't think there are any good reasons to ship precompiled binaries linked against GNU libc. It usually ends up with problems and ugly hacks.
I'm facing the exact same issue.

I looked into the code and found the root cause: when restoring a session, `restoreSessionStateFromMessages()` reads the last user message's agent and writes it into session state. Then `resolveModeState()` sees a non-empty `storedModeId` and returns early, skipping `default_agent` entirely.

I think restoring the last-used agent is actually good idea — if you were mid-task in Build mode, coming back to Build makes sense. But it does ignore users who have explicitly configured `default_agent` and expect it to always be respected.

I'm thinking through the best way to handle this and will share a concrete proposal soon.

Still hitting this on v1.15.4 (Windows). Custom provider using `@ai-sdk/openai` with `baseURL` override — model is `gpt-5.5` which is multimodal, but OpenCode reports `capabilities.input.image: false`.

Tried every config-level workaround I could find:
- Adding `vision: true` to the model definition — ignored
- Adding `capabilities: { input: { image: true } }` — ignored
- Adding `attachment: true` — sets `capabilities.attachment: true` but `input.image` stays false
- Switching npm adapter from `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` to `@ai-sdk/openai` — no change
- Using a model ID that OpenCode recognizes (`gpt-4o`) under the custom provider — still false

The capability registry appears to be entirely hardcoded in the Go binary and ignores user config overrides. This makes **all** custom/proxy providers unable to use image input regardless of the model's actual capabilities.

Would love to see either:
1. A config-level `capabilities` override that the registry respects, or
2. The registry updated to include `gpt-5.5` (released by OpenAI, multimodal)

Thanks for the great project otherwise!
